newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable, overnight dollar soars.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable, overnight dollar soars.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in early trading on Monday, but overnight dollar deposit rates soared, dealers said.
They said volume was quite thin and trading was limited to commercial orders. They said no position was taken.
"This is the last trading day of the year. We just take on some commercial orders," one foreign bank dealer said.
Dealers said operators were squeezed on overnight dollars following some tightening and rises in offshore markets.
Overnight dollar deposit rates soared to 11.0 percent at 0300 GMT, compared with some 5.5 percent in an usual day.
One local bank dealer said rises of overnight dollars in offshore markets seemed to have aided the sharp local increase.

He also attributed the rise to year-end factors as banks had to close the books, which forced them to take on any rate available. Dealers said ample rupiah supply at the year-end continued to depress interbank rates and soften swap premiums.
Overnight swap fell to -0.15/par from 0.25/0.35 points.
Dealers said there was no mood to trade in the market and many dealing rooms will only be opened for half the day.
The foreign exchange market will be closed on December 31 and January 1, and will resume trading on January 2.
Spot rupiah was at 2,363.50/63.75 at 0305 GMT against an opening of 2,363.00/64.25. Tomorrow was at 2,363.0/63.5.
Today rupiah was last given at 2,365.0.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention rate at 2,358/2,550 and the conversion rate at 2,358/2,406 last Friday.
